arStrings.szText:
Neyrelle sits on a small boat chanting in the old Horadric tongue and clutching the soulstone tight. She sweats and shakes as she struggles to contain the stone. Black ichor leaks from it, staining her fingers. Concerned, the boatman offers his help. When he reaches out to touch her shoulder, she explodes. "Stay away from me!"

All of a sudden, she hears the voice of her mother, Vhenard. "Neyrelle! Is that how I raised you?" The stone hovers in front of her face. Neyrelle, chastised, explains she must carry the soulstone alone. Vhenard, now present, tenderly voices her concern that Neyrelle's burden is killing her. She cups her daughter's face and comforts her. "I'm here, little magpie. I'm so proud of you. But now, I need you to give up."

Vhenard's flesh turns black with ichor. Neyrelle starts with realization. "Of course it's you! You monster!" Mephisto. He pulls Neyrelle further into her vision, one where she is suspended in a web of blood and tissue, all her limbs pulled taut. "You made a choice. And I warned you, little magpie, there would be consequences." The sinews that bind her limbs rip them open, splitting each down the middle. She screams in agony. Mephisto orders her to surrender, but she fights fiercely not to give in.

All at once, she comes back to herself, sitting on the boat, her limbs still in one piece. She shudders as she calms. "Maybe you're right. Maybe I could use some help." She turns to face the boatman, but finds that he is dead, speared through the chest by a massive tendril of ichor. She holds back tears as she resumes her chant, takes up his oar, and continues down the river into Nahantu.

The Reverend Mother Prava addresses her flock. She introduces the Burned Knight Urivar who, like her, is a survivor of the battle in Hell. Urivar wears a porcelain mask that covers extensive burn scars. Another Knight leads a bound man before the crowd and pushes him to his knees. Urivar condemns the bound man, a mercenary in the service of Lorath, for trying to hide Neyrelle from the Cathedral's judgment.

Prava asks the mercenary if he repents of his sins. Desperate to live, he eagerly repents. Prava orders his release. But Urivar interrupts. "Father Inarius' mercy was great, but did he not also preach justice?" Against Prava's will, he riles up the crowd until they too scream for justice. The mercenary begs for his life to no avail. Urivar picks up a torch and sets him on fire.

Raheir invites the Wanderer to sit while he and his young daughter, Fayira, work on finishing a shield. The Wanderer asks after Neyrelle. Raheir reveals that she passed through town a few weeks ago, on the waw to Nahantu. The Wanderer is taken aback. Raheir knew that she carried the soulstone, yet he just let her go off alone. "You didn't even offer to help her? What is wrong with you?" Raheir tactfully asks Fayira to retrieve a tool for him. After she leaves, he explains that she is his adopted daughter. She and all of Gea Kul are a responsibility he's taken onto his shoulders, just as the Wanderer and the Horadrim have chosen to carry Sanctuary on theirs. "I will not trade one for another. Would you?"

Chastened, the Wanderer says no. Raheir respects their anger. "You care too much, my friend. But that is a glad thing." He offers his aid to them. Suddenly, the sounds of battle erupt from outside the workshop. Raheir grows serious. "They've returned."

The Wanderer watches as Varyana kneels next to Grelkar's corpse. She pulls out her dagger and plunges it into the body. With effort, she begins to carve it open. Curled over the corpse, she tosses out an organ here, a wet chunk of flesh there, chanting in a strange language. The Wanderer steps forward in concern. "Varyana? What's happening? This is... it's too much. You don't need to do this to yourself." Her response is hissed. "Don't look at me."

At last, she stands, holding up the liver. She bites into it and violently tears it apart. Suddenly, she seizes, taken by visions. "Zolmog… Tyrant King… crown of teeth… throne of bone… king of flesh made flesh…  Zolmog anointed in Guulrahn…" She shakes and pants in exhaustion as she comes back to herself. Her visions have set her course: "We go to Guulrahn. Now."

The Wanderer examines a doll while a creature watches from the rafters above. It shouts, "Leave!" The Wanderer demands to know what it's done with the boy. In a burst of flame, the creature hops down to face them. He is small, with clawed feet and demonic horns. "He's dead! I tore him apart." He takes an interest in a doll. "Where did you get that?"

The Wanderer asks if the doll is his. Warily, the boy approaches with palms held out. "It was a gift from Father... please." He snatches the doll and runs to a dark corner of the room. The Wanderer wonders where his father is, but receives no answer. Unable to leave a child alone, they ask the boy to come with them. He's nervous to leave. "You saw what happened. When I get scared... the monsters appear." The Wanderer assuages his fear, saying that they know of a place he needn't be scared. A place with good people.

The boy hesitantly asks if the Wanderer will be there too. "Of course I will."

A prisoner lies bound on an altar, surrounded by three bandits. The ringleader stands before the altar, holding a dagger high, poised to make a killing strike. But the Wanderer interrupts. "You're... bandits? You're cultists!" They say in realization. The ringleader threatens them, saying they're outnumbered, but suddenly, arrows fly out of the darkness and stab the two other cultists. 

Subo steps out of the shadows. He offers the ringleader a chance to run. "Leave. And live." But the cultist chooses to fight. Subo looses three more arrows, killing him swiftly. He gets to work freeing the prisoner. The Wanderer is irritated he failed to inform them this was a rescue mission. His response is dismissive. "I assumed you were paying attention. And everything worked out fine, didn't it?" The two prepare to leave. But before they do, the altar bubbles with dark energy. It breaks apart in a mess of rubble to reveal a demon, summoned from the blood spilt there. They will have to fight.

The Hatred corruption melts away from the Akarat lion as he collapses, spent. Neyrelle rushes over to him. "Shhh. It's all right. I know you need to go now. You've done more for me than I could ever imagine. I promise... I won't forget. I promise I won't give up." She cradles his head gently. "It's time for you to go."

The lion dissipates into golden light, revealing Akarat's human spirit form. "When death first came for me, the embrace of the Spirit Realm awaited. But now.... Now, I am afraid. Remember this in the days to come... that, in the end, Akarat was afraid." Neyrelle tearfully asks if she will ever see him again, to which he says yes. His spirit fades away, leaving Neyrelle alone with her tears.

Eru, haggard and injured, walks out to meet the Wanderer and Neyrelle. Neyrelle demands to know what Mephisto gave Eru in exchange for his betrayal. He admits that the Prime Evil swore to spare Nahantu and the Spirit Realm from his corruption. "Even knowing I will never see it... I would not unmake my choices."

Neyrelle warns him that Mephisto always breaks his promises. "Just tell us what you did with the stone and the body. We can still make this right." Eru explodes in frustration. "There is no making this right." He goes on to say that he chose to break their trust, and every day after, he must choose to do it again by withholding that information. He doesn't believe he's strong enough to do that.

So he's come here, to offer the Wanderer and Neyrelle their vengeance. He prepares to fight, to die. Neyrelle fires off a bolt of magic at him. In his wounded state, it's enough to knock him out.

The Wanderer approaches the corpse of Ah Bulan, but Eru stops them. "No. I was the one who failed Ah Bulan." He kneels beside the massive body, singing a mournful dirge in the Nahantu language. He pulls out his ritual digger and begins to carve open the spirit's chest. The light of spirit magic emanates from the wound. He reaches inside, and with tender care, pulls out the glowing heart of Ah Bulan. He passes it to the Wanderer.

Eru places his hands on the once-great spirit, sobbing through the last words of his song.

At the stone pillars, Eru and Maka begin to chant in the Nahantu language. A magical surface shimmers between the pillars--the makings of a portal. When the Wanderer walks up to the surface, they see a reflection of themselves on the other side. Maka walks around the stones and grasps the empty air there. She suddenly drives a knife into the air. The Wanderer screams out in pain as their reflection is stabbed.

Eru coaches them to let the pain carry them through, instead of fighting it. Maka twists the blade and Eru pushes the Wanderer into the portal.

In the Durance of Hate, Akarat's corpse lies surrounded by statues of his Dedicants. The black ichor of Mephisto's corruption stains the floor and fills the circle, submerging Akarat's body. The ichor seizes once, twice, three times, before settling again. Now, Akarat rises from the pool, baptized in black sludge as he is born anew. Hovering, he opens eyes devoid of pupils.

Mephisto speaks. "Wrapped in the guise of man, I shall walk amongst the innocent. And there will be no salvation in the Light."

Akarat's corpse lays at the center of a dais, perfectly preserved inside the Vault of Light. Neyrelle approaches with the soulstone in hand. She kneels before him, hesitant. The Wanderer stands nearby in support. "You can let go now."

She turns to them, determination in her face. She places the stone at the center of Akarat's chest and a wave of light pulses outwards from him. Slowly, the tendrils of Hatred that plagued her begin to recede from her skin.

For the first time in a long time, Neyrelle smiles.

While the Wanderer gazes over the edge of the bridge at the dead boatman below, Urivar approaches from behind. He commends all that the Wanderer has done for the church--even though they traffic in darkness. He threateningly asks of Neyrelle's whereabouts. When the Wanderer refuses to help him, two more Knights drag in Raheir, bloodied and beaten. He's missing his right arm--all that remains is a smoldering stump. Urivar presses. "How many lives will you trade to protect Neyrelle? Is her life worth more than his?"

The Wanderer prepares to fight, but they are distracted by the sound of Neyrelle's voice. They turn to see a vision of her on the river, chanting a Horadric chant, protecting the soulstone. Urivar approaches from behind and suddenly stabs them in the back. "No one is above the laws of Heaven." He kicks the Wanderer over the ledge of the bridge and they plunge into the river below.

As they float down the river, we see a portion of Rathma's prophecy:
I saw my corpse, 
and from my mouth crawled Hatred, 
A father burned his children on a pyre, 
And a mother molded a new age from the ashes, 
I saw the weak made strong, 
a pack of lambs feasting on wolves, 
Tears of blood rained upon a desert jewel, 
and the way to Hell was torn asunder, 
Then came a spear of light, piercing Hatred’s heart, 
And he who was bound in chains was set free. 

A short time later, the Wanderer lies unconscious on the river bank. An old man runs up to them and summons magic into his palms, pushing life back into their body. They wake gasping.

Inside the Vault of Light, the Wanderer thanks Eru for his help. But he only replies, "Don't." He kneels at the other side of the dais, dripping blood, his sacrificial knife on the ground. The Akarat lion roars as Eru lifts his head to show a bloody circle of ritual cuts on his face. "I do this for Nahantu. Spirits, forgive me."

Dark magic pulses through him and a rift opens in the Vault. Explosive waves of energy pulse through the room, throwing everyone backwards. The lion lies prone on the ground. As the Wanderer recovers, Neyrelle screams that Eru has the stone. He stands before the rift, Akarat's corpse cradled in his arms. The inner conflict is clear on his face. "You deserve better from me." But he turns away, to face the hulking shape of the Harbinger of Hatred. "I've done my part. See that you do yours." He leaves through the portal, taking the stone and Akarat's corpse with him.

The Harbinger stalks forward, larger and more monstrous than ever. The Wanderer screams in anger. He relishes their fury--their hatred. "One moment of betrayal and my blood sings in you. Few mortals are so worthy of their birthright. Come, child of my child. I will give you the violence you long for."

Neyrelle sits alone atop a pillar, crouched over the soulstone, chanting in the Horadric tongue hoarse and low. When she sees the Wandere, her voice quavers with emotion, though her chant never stops. The Wanderer is horrified. "Neyrelle... what has Mephisto done to you?"

The Herald of Hatred stalks out from the shadows. His form is massive, over twice the size it was before. "We have each played a part in what has happened here." He speaks of when they last met, in Hell, when the Wanderer left Mephisto's fate to Neyrelle. "You abdicated your choice to this child, and she has already been poisoned by the stone."

The stone responds to Mephisto, humming and floating with energy. Neyrelle's chant intensifies as she struggles to control it. "She will die before she surrenders. A wasteful outcome for both of us. How long do you think she can survive?"

Suddenly, a golden lion drops down into the fray. It roars menacingly, emanating the light of spirit magic. The demons that had attacked the Wanderer before are killed instantly. Eru whispers with emotion, "Akarat."

The lion turns to the Wanderer. "Only she can unmake her prison. Seek Ah Bulan, for he has strength to lend her."

Urivar stumbles back, drenched in his own blood. Gurgling, he hisses out a portion of Rathma's prophecy. He drops all pretense. "That fool, Inarius, dragged the Cathedral into Hell because of a poem scribbled out by a half-breed abomination." He turns his ire to the Wanderer next. "Then you escort that girl to our destruction and call it righteous. And you think I am the one who is mad?"

He lays down his sword and takes off his mask. Passionate, he says he offered the people order and salvation. He kneels and opens his arms in invitation for the end.

"What do you offer?"

Neyrelle's chant is hoarse and low, her gaze unfocused and half-lidded. It takes all the strength she has left to contain the soulstone, which floats independently before her. The Wanderer approaches with the heart of Ah Bulan and explains that consuming it will free her. They kneel to her level. "Neyrelle... It's me. I'm here for you. You don't have to keep doing this alone." She gasps shakily, seemingly aware now. The Akarat lion steps near, offering his support too.

With determination, she grasps the heart and bites into it. She struggles to chew and swallow its pieces, gagging on the viscera. When her strength returns, the soulstone clatters to the ground, tamed once more. It hovers obediently into her outstretched hand.

The lion offers his back. Neyrelle climbs atop him, free to ride out of the Durance of Hate at last.
